- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 3–8% from forecast for 2–3 periods.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast toward historical mean or 14-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early downward momentum; if sentiment turns negative within 5 days, adjust forecast downward by 3–7% starting from day 5.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead, not lagging 3–5 days.
